latest_release.name: v1.13.0
latest_release.body:
## Pro highlights

These features are in [It's a Plan Pro](https://itsaplan.dev/pro).

### Workflow improvements

- Stop a run with Cancel run, also from the run lists. This also stops the agent runs of its steps. The run shows who canceled it.
- Resume a canceled run. Finished steps keep their results.
- Run a workflow from the canvas or from any trigger. A webhook trigger takes a request that you write.
- The canvas has a new algorithm for connections. It draws them together, in right angles around the steps, with fewer crossings.
- The canvas has a tour, uses your color theme, and shows one panel at a time. The panels have sections that fold.

### Agents run workflows

An internal agent can run the workflows of its project. The agent needs the Run workflows action, which is off by default, and a role that can edit workflows.

### Exa tools for agents

With an [Exa](https://exa.ai) key, agents search the web, read pages, and answer questions with sources.

## Community highlights

### Repository issues on the board

A connected GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, or Forgejo repository sends its issues to the board. With one-way sync, new issues appear on the board. When you close or reopen one, the repository issue closes or reopens too. With two-way sync, changes in the repository also update the board issue. You can also import open issues, map labels, and copy new comments.

### New Docs

The page tree stays open next to each page. The Docs home shows comment threads that wait for you, pinned pages, and recent pages. One popover sets who can open a page: the project, specific people, or only you. It also sets the public link.

### AI chat and agent runs in one panel

One side panel shows the AI chat and the agent runs of the open project. Press `C` for the chat and `R` for the runs.

### Stop an agent run

Stop an agent run from its page, the API, or MCP (`cancel_agent_run`). The run shows who stopped it. Runner 0.9.0 also kills the command of a stopped run.

### Slack

Members get notifications as Slack direct messages. Agents send and read Slack messages with the Slack tools. To configure the app, see [Slack notifications](https://github.com/croffasia/itsaplan/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md#slack-notifications).

### All notification settings on one page

The Notifications page in the account menu has the channels, the defaults, and the settings of each project. A project uses the defaults until you change it. You can change several projects at once. The settings that you already have do not change.

### GitLab, pull request, and [Baserow](https://baserow.io) tools for agents

Agents review and merge pull requests on GitHub, Gitea, and Forgejo. The new GitLab tools do the same for merge requests and also work with issues. With [Baserow](https://baserow.io), agents read and change table rows.

## Also in this release

- In Pro, a person's usage and budget include the runs that agents start for that person.
- In Pro, the agent usage of a schedule or a workflow can include the runs that its agents started.
- In Pro, the audit log records each stopped agent run.
- In Pro, people who can read the steps of a project's runs also see the HTTP tool calls.
- A team owner is an owner of each project of the team. A team manager can read each project, use the AI chat, and see agent runs, without a project membership.
- The interface, Pro screens included, and the Community emails are available in Italian. Language lists show each language by its own name.
- You can add an initiative to your favorites in the sidebar. The command palette finds initiatives.
- The Docs tree starts collapsed and keeps the branches that you open. A button expands or collapses all branches.
- You can move a Docs page from its menu, without dragging. A resolved Docs comment shows who resolved it. A table lists the archived pages.
- When you add a link in the editor, a form opens in the text. The mention menu g

# The open-source Linear alternative
where AI agents take issues like teammates Use it as a regular issue tracker from day one. When you are ready, give an agent an issue the way you give it to a colleague, and review the result yourself or let another agent check it. Put agents on a schedule, or build a workflow that passes an issue from agent to agent. Self-hosted, on your own server. If It's a Plan looks useful to you, star the repo ⭐ and [leave a review on Product Hunt](https://www.producthunt.com/products/it-s-a-plan/reviews).
For news and updates, [follow us on Threads](https://www.threads.com/@itsaplandev). **Trusted by** [All teams](ADOPTERS.md) · [Add your team →](https://itsaplan.dev/account/showcase)
## Why It's a Plan - **Agents as project members.** Each gets a role, permissions and an assignee slot, and works on the same board as your people. - **Two kinds of agents.** Internal agents run on your server, on any model with your API key. External agents run on your machine through [`@itsaplan/runner`](packages/runner), under your own Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI or opencode account. - **Any kind of work.** Software, marketing, design, support, sales, operations, research. - **Yours to run.** Your server and your database. ## Community features | Area | What you get | | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Product management | Kanban, table, timeline, and calendar views · cycles · custom fields · dashboards · docs · notes boards · project templates · import from Linear, Trello, and Plane | | AI agents | Agents as project members · internal on any model, or external on your coding CLI · runs start on an @mention, an assignment, or a schedule | | Platform | REST API with OpenAPI · MCP server · webhooks · pull requests from 5 forges · SSO over OIDC and SCIM · passkeys and Google sign-in | | 14 languages | English · Українська · Русский · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · العربية · Français · فارسی · Português (Brasil) · Bahasa Indonesia · Español · 한국어 · Türkçe · Italiano |
Product management: the full list - Configure issues per project: custom fields, labels, states, and issue types - Kanban, table, timeline, and calendar views. Save a view as a tab with its own filters, fields, and two-level grouping, for the whole project or only for you. Each person orders and hides their own tabs - Cycles that time-box the work. Unfinished issues move to the next cycle - Subtasks, checklists, attachments, and links between issues: blocks, relates, duplicates - Comment threads with replies, and @mentions of people and agents - Project dashboards: throughput, burnup with a projected completion date, breakdown, and pulse - Quick actions on an issue, and automatic assignment when an issue moves to a state - Docs: Markdown pages in a tree, with revision history, private and locked pages, embedded files, comments, @mentions, and links to issues - Notes boards: sticky notes on a canvas, with colors, checklists, and connections - Share a view, an issue, or a document by public link, read-only and without sign-in - Initiatives that group and track related work inside a project - Project templates: save a project as a template for your team, or publish it to the gallery at itsaplan.dev - Import projects from [Linear](docs/importing-from-linear.md), [Trello](docs/importing-from-trello.md), and [Plane](docs/importing-from-plane.md) - Auto-archive, a notification inbox, and role-based access control
AI agents: the full list - Agents as project members, with their own permissions and assigned issues - Internal agents run on the instance. Configure the model, system prompt, tools, and reusable skills, written inline or imported from a GitHub repository - External agents run on your machine, under your own account. [`@itsaplan/runner`](packages/runner) gives each task to Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, opencode, Pi, Oh My Pi, Mastra Code, or any command that reads stdin - Your own code can also take tasks from the run queue through the API - A run starts on an @mention in a comment on an issue or a document, on an assignment, or on a schedule. A schedule starts on a timer or when an issue moves to a state - Tokens and cost of every run, by agent, project, and model - Tools for other services: Notion, Baserow, Telegram, Slack, Threads, Instagram, Jina, Firecrawl, Keenable, DataForSEO, Gitea, Forgejo, GitHub, and GitLab - Images, video, music, and speech from the models on [Kie](https://kie.ai?ref=0b6eb19939298accdf58e18b1a92a26e): Nano Banana, Seedream, Kling, Veo, Suno, and others, with one API key - Chat with each agent, with its own history. Turn chat off for an agent that only works on mentions, assignments, and schedules - Chat with an external agent too. The runner answers from your machine, streams the reply and its tool calls, and resumes the same coding agent session on each message
Platform: the full list - REST API with an OpenAPI reference and API keys - MCP server, so an external assistant can read and change issues through the same API - Pull requests from GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, and Bitbucket. "Fixes KEY-42" links the pull request to the issue, and the issue moves when the pull request opens and merges - Outgoing webhooks for the events you pick, with signed payloads, retries, and a delivery log - Sign-in with an email or username and a password, a passkey, Google, or your identity provider over OIDC. SCIM keeps accounts in sync with your directory - Notifications by email (SMTP, Resend, or Microsoft 365), Telegram, and Slack, with preferences for each member - Instance administration: storage limits, the mail provider, and instance-wide settings
## Pro edition Bring the whole team. Pro adds full control over workspaces, agents and spend. > [!TIP] > **$240 a year for the whole instance, 1 person or 500.** Fast Deploy installs Pro on your own > server in about 5 minutes. Everything in Community, plus: - Fast Deploy - Unlimited workspaces - SAML or OIDC per workspace - SCIM per workspace - Workspace dashboard - Audit log - Agent workflows - Schedules on issue events - Agent cost by person, trigger and workflow - AI budgets - Public forms [See what each feature does →](https://itsaplan.dev/pro) Three ways to run Pro: - **[Fast Deploy](https://itsaplan.dev/pro#fast-deploy)** installs Pro on your own Hetzner, Vultr or DigitalOcean server in about 5 minutes. Updates take one click. - **[Railway](docs/railway.md):** the template runs Pro in one click. - **By hand:** deploy on [Docker](docs/self-hosting.md), [Coolify](docs/coolify.md) or [Kubernetes](docs/helm.md). On Railway and by hand, enter the key in god mode under **License**. Without a valid key, Pro runs as Community. Your data stays when you switch editions. ## Getting started ### Deploy on Railway — recommended [![Deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/button.svg)](https://railway.com/deploy/its-a-plan?referralCode=lQ5O6i&utm_medium=integration&utm_source=button&utm_campaign=itsaplan) The whole stack in one click, with no server to maintain. You give Railway two hostnames, and it generates every secret. You need a domain of your own: [the guide](docs/railway.md) explains why, and what to do after the deploy. ### Fast Deploy for Pro With a Pro license, [Fast Deploy](https://itsaplan.dev/account/hosting) installs Pro on a new server in your Hetzner, Vultr or DigitalOcean account. See [Pro edition](#pro-edition). ### Try it on your machine Requirements: Docker and [Bun](https://bun.sh). ```bash git clone https://github.com/croffasia/itsaplan.git cd itsaplan bun install bun run setup # answer "Try it" ``` It picks free ports, generates the secrets, starts the whole stack in Docker, and opens . Everything runs on localhost, so no domain and no reverse proxy are needed. Run it again later to restart the instance; the data stays. ### Everything else - [Deploy on Railway](docs/railway.md) — one-click hosted deploy from the template - [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md) — the full production setup, secrets, and updates - [Deploy on Coolify](docs/coolify.md) — the same stack on a Coolify instance - [Deploy on Kubernetes](docs/helm.md) — Helm chart for any Kubernetes cluster - [Local development](docs/development.md) — running the apps on the host, and the tests - [Coding agent setup](docs/runner.md) — the config for each CLI that `@itsaplan/runner` runs - [Agent endpoint](docs/agent-endpoint.md) — the instance sends an external agent's tasks to a URL that you run, such as an AWS Lambda function ## Built with | Layer | Technology | | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | Runtime | [Bun](https://bun.sh) + [Turborepo](https://turbo.build) | | Backend | [Elysia](https://elysiajs.com/) | | Frontend | [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) App Router, SSR | | UI | [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) + Tailwind v4 | | Auth | [better-auth](https://better-auth.com/) | | Database | [Drizzle](https://orm.drizzle.team/) + PostgreSQL | | Storage | S3-compatible object store (RustFS) | | AI agents | [Mastra](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra) | ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome — bug fixes, features, docs, all of it. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). It covers the setup, the conventions, and how a change gets merged. Be kind; we follow a [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Thank you to everyone who has contributed to It's a Plan: Not ready to contribute code? [Star the repo](https://github.com/croffasia/itsaplan) and share it — it is the simplest way to help the project grow. ## Security Found a vulnerability? Report it privately through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/croffasia/itsaplan/security/advisories/new), not a public issue, so we can fix it first. Details in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License Copyright © 2026 Andrii Poluosmak. [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE), except `packages/runner`, which is [Apache-2.0](packages/runner/LICENSE). A commercial licence is available if AGPL-3.0 does not fit your company. Ask on [Telegram](https://telegram.me/croffasia).
